The '''Cotlar–Stein almost orthogonality lemma''' is a [[mathematical lemma]] in the field of [[functional analysis]]. It may be used to obtain information on the [[operator norm]] on an [[operator (mathematics)|operator]], acting from one [[Hilbert space]] into another, when the operator can be decomposed into ''almost orthogonal'' pieces. 

The original version of this lemma (for [[self-adjoint]] and mutually [[Commutative property|commuting]] operators) was proved by [[Mischa Cotlar]] in 1955<ref>{{harvnb|Cotlar|1955}}</ref> and allowed him to conclude that the [[Hilbert transform]] is a [[continuous linear operator]] in [[Square-integrable function|<math>L^2</math>]] without using the [[Fourier transform]]. A more general version was proved by [[Elias M. Stein|Elias Stein]].<ref>{{harvnb|Stein|1993}}</ref>

==Statement of the lemma==
Let <math>E,\,F</math> be two [[Hilbert spaces]]. Consider a family of operators <math>T_j</math>, <math> j\geq 1</math>, with each <math>T_j</math> a [[bounded linear operator]] from <math>E</math> to <math>F</math>.

Denote

: <math>a_{jk}=\Vert T_j T_k^\ast\Vert,
\qquad b_{jk}=\Vert T_j^\ast T_k\Vert.</math>

The family of operators <math>T_j:\;E\to F</math>, <math>j\ge 1,</math> is ''almost orthogonal'' if

:<math>A=\sup_{j}\sum_{k}\sqrt{a_{jk}}<\infty,
\qquad B=\sup_{j}\sum_{k}\sqrt{b_{jk}}<\infty.</math>

The Cotlar–Stein lemma states that if <math>T_j</math> are almost orthogonal, then the series <math>\sum_{j}T_j</math> converges in the [[strong operator topology]], and

:<math>\Vert \sum_{j}T_j\Vert \le\sqrt{AB}.</math>

==Proof==
If <math>T_1,\ldots,T_n</math> is a finite collection of bounded operators, then<ref>{{harvnb|Hörmander|1994}}</ref> (as will be proven below)

:<math>\displaystyle{\sum_{i,j} |(T_i v,T_jv)| \le \left(\max_i \sum_j \|T_i^*T_j\|^{1\over 2}\right)\left(\max_i \sum_j \|T_iT_j^*\|^{1\over 2}\right)\|v\|^2.}</math>

So under the hypotheses of the lemma,

:<math>\displaystyle{\sum_{i,j} |(T_i v,T_jv)| \le AB\|v\|^2.}</math>

It follows that 

:<math>\displaystyle{\|\sum_{i=1}^n T_iv\|^2 \le AB \|v\|^2,}</math>

and that

:<math>\displaystyle{\|\sum_{i=m}^n T_iv\|^2 \le \sum_{i,j\ge m} |(T_iv,T_jv)|.}</math>

Hence, the partial sums 

:<math>\displaystyle{s_n=\sum_{i=1}^n T_iv}</math>

form a [[Cauchy sequence]]. 

The sum is therefore [[Absolute convergence|absolutely convergent]] with the limit satisfying the stated inequality.

To prove the inequality above set

:<math>\displaystyle{R=\sum a_{ij}T_i^*T_j}</math>

with |''a''<sub>''ij''</sub>| ≤ 1 chosen so that

:<math>\displaystyle{(Rv,v)=|(Rv,v)|=\sum |(T_iv,T_jv)|.}</math>

Then

:<math>\displaystyle{\|R\|^{2m} =\|(R^*R)^m\|\le \sum \|T_{i_1}^* T_{i_2} T_{i_3}^* T_{i_4} \cdots T_{i_{4m}}\| \le \sum \left(\|T_{i_1}^*\|\|T_{i_1}^*T_{i_2}\|\|T_{i_2}T_{i_3}^*\|\cdots \|T_{i_{4m-1}}^* T_{i_{4m}}\|\|T_{i_{4m}}\|\right)^{1\over 2}.}</math>

Hence

:<math>\displaystyle{\|R\|^{2m} \le n \cdot \max \|T_i\| \left(\max_i \sum_j \|T_i^*T_j\|^{1\over 2}\right)^{2m}\left(\max_i \sum_j \|T_iT_j^*\|^{1\over 2}\right)^{2m-1}.}</math>

Taking 2''m''th roots and letting ''m'' tend to ∞,

:<math>\displaystyle{\|R\|\le  \left(\max_i \sum_j \|T_i^*T_j\|^{1\over 2}\right)\left(\max_i \sum_j \|T_iT_j^*\|^{1\over 2}\right),}</math>

which immediately implies the inequality.

==Generalization==
The Cotlar-Stein lemma has been generalized, with sums being replaced by integrals.<ref>{{harvnb|Knapp|Stein|1971}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Calderon|first1=Alberto|last2=Vaillancourt|first2=Remi|title=On the boundedness of pseudo-differential operators|journal=Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan|date=1971|volume=23|issue=2|pages=374–378|doi=10.2969/jmsj/02320374|doi-access=free}}</ref> Let ''X'' be a [[locally compact space]] and μ a [[Borel measure]] on ''X''. Let ''T''(''x'') be a map from ''X'' into bounded operators from ''E'' to ''F'' which is uniformly bounded and continuous in the strong operator topology. If 

:<math>\displaystyle{A= \sup_x \int_X \|T(x)^*T(y)\|^{1\over 2} \, d\mu(y),\,\,\, B= \sup_x \int_X \|T(y)T(x)^*\|^{1\over 2}\, d\mu(y),}</math>

are finite, then the function ''T''(''x'')''v'' is integrable for each ''v'' in ''E'' with

:<math>\displaystyle{\|\int_X T(x)v\, d\mu(x)\| \le \sqrt{AB}  \cdot \|v\|.}</math>

The result can be proven by replacing sums with integrals in the previous proof, or by utilizing Riemann sums to approximate the integrals.

==Example==
Here is an example of an orthogonal family of operators. Consider the infinite-dimensional matrices.

:<math>
T=\left[
\begin{array}{cccc}
1&0&0&\vdots\\0&1&0&\vdots\\0&0&1&\vdots\\\cdots&\cdots&\cdots&\ddots\end{array}
\right]
</math>

and also

:<math>
\qquad
T_1=\left[
\begin{array}{cccc}
1&0&0&\vdots\\0&0&0&\vdots\\0&0&0&\vdots\\\cdots&\cdots&\cdots&\ddots\end{array}
\right],
\qquad
T_2=\left[
\begin{array}{cccc}
0&0&0&\vdots\\0&1&0&\vdots\\0&0&0&\vdots\\\cdots&\cdots&\cdots&\ddots\end{array}
\right],
\qquad
T_3=\left[
\begin{array}{cccc}
0&0&0&\vdots\\0&0&0&\vdots\\0&0&1&\vdots\\\cdots&\cdots&\cdots&\ddots\end{array}
\right],
\qquad
\dots.
</math>

Then <math>\Vert T_j\Vert=1</math> for each <math>j</math>, hence the series <math>\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}T_j</math> does not converge in the [[uniform operator topology]].

Yet, since
<math>\Vert T_j T_k^\ast\Vert=0</math>
and 
<math>\Vert T_j^\ast T_k\Vert=0</math>
for <math>j\ne k</math>, 
the Cotlar–Stein almost orthogonality lemma tells us that 

:<math>T=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}T_j</math>

converges in the [[strong operator topology]] and is bounded by 1.
